newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares close fractionally mixed.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares close fractionally mixed.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed mixed in light trade with a dearth of news depriving the market of any sense of direction, said traders.
The bolsa is seen continuing to drift at the opening, although quarter-end portfolio shuffling could add an element of volatility, they said.
"Unfortunately there are no variations in structural factors which point to a change in mood," said one broker.
The 40-share IPSA index ended up 0.05 percent at 99.02 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.26 percent at 5,432.23 points amid volume of 10 billion pesos.
Traders noted that average daily turnover has fallen by half since the Central Bank first jacked up interest rates late last year to cool rapid economic growth.

The bolsa failed to find encouragement in news that Bankers Trust boosted its Chilean weighting to 10 percent from 7.6 percent after slashing its Argentine weighting to almost zero from 5.6 percent, they said.

Forestry firm Copec gained on speculation that its pulp division Celulosa Arauco y Constitucion (Celco) offered the highest bid in the privatization for Argentine pulp plant Alto Parana, said traders.
Evening newspaper La Segunda said Celco bid $250 million with the other Chilean bidder CMPC offering $190 million.
Both companies declined comment. The official result of the sale, which is being handled by Goldman Sachs, is expected to be announced next week.
Copec closed up 0.8 percent at 1,775 pesos, while CMPC shed 0.38 percent at 5,200 pesos.
Other losers included power utility Endesa, down 0.57 percent at 260 pesos, and bottler Andina, which declined 0.42 percent to 2,350 pesos.
Winners included telecom Telex, up 0.86 percent at 1,170 pesos, and steel-maker Cap, which rose 0.76 percent to 1,330 pesos.
